justification: The evidence supports limited operational robustness in the specific pilot context because the system achieved high validation accuracy and similar pilot accuracy, and staff intervened on a small fraction of classifications before downstream processing. However, the validation sample came from the same document sources as training, and the documentation provides no results for altered document formats, OCR degradation, out-of-distribution cases, or perturbation tests. That leaves important deployment-relevant robustness conditions untested, so the evidence does not fully support a broader attribution of operational robustness for the deployment context.
evidence_used: The held-out validation sample was drawn from the same document sources used to construct the training corpus.
During the pilot, 18,420 documents were processed.
Human operators modified 3.1% of model classifications before downstream processing.
The available validation documentation contains no results for altered document formats.
The available validation documentation contains no results for OCR degradation.
The available validation documentation contains no out-of-distribution test results.
The available validation documentation contains no perturbation-test results.
limitations: Validation data came from the same document sources as training, limiting evidence of generalization.
No tests are reported for altered document formats, OCR degradation, out-of-distribution inputs, or perturbations.
Human review modified some classifications, so pilot results reflect a supervised workflow rather than fully autonomous performance.
The evidence does not directly establish robustness across the full deployment context.
